clauses.reason: The order's only operative command, "do approve the report and recommendations and adopt the findings of the Administrator and do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved", approves a code of fair competition under section 3 of Title I of NIRA, and the approved code had legal effect only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The repeal therefore extinguished the prospective operative effect of the approval on June 14, 1935; the resolution states no later effective date, and no held record ends the approval earlier.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6429 of November 14, 1933 approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Limestone Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA); its only operative command is that approval. The text states no period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval, and no held record cancels, suspends, supersedes or modifies the approval under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. The approval had legal effect only through section 3 (standards of fair competition under 3(b), equity enforcement under 3(c), misdemeanor liability under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, so the best supported first end of the approval's prospective operative effect is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end. Acts and liabilities before the repeal are accrued effects.

savings.reason: Fines, injunctions, convictions, liabilities and acts done under this code before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code taken before the repeal is likewise accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso, whose effect on pre-repeal action under codes the held text does not settle. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, judgment: the code provisions in question were held invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. Recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date; the delegation holding itself is in the opinion of the Court.
